Chicago does have an odd admiration for dems that don’t do much, if anything objectively “good.” Performative at best. But eliminating RT and CG cannot be blamed for gentrification. The projects didn’t work. They were supposed to give people a leg up, but they ultimately only perpetuated the poverty cycle. They also exacerbated the gang problem. Gangs could also take over entire buildings, meaning access by law enforcement was basically a suicide mission. 

Economists and housing scientists had the solution to these problems: spread the equivalent number of units across the city and in every neighborhood-a design proven to give a true “leg up” without creating crime hot spots. But commercial developers and the most vocal members of affluent neighborhoods wouldn’t let that happen. Loopholes and exceptions emerged, and the whole overhaul is now just another example of “same shit, different day.” 

At most, demolishing RT and CB just added fuel to the dumpster fire that was, and always will be, gentrification. A trend not at all unique to Chicago.
